Theorem 7 (Correct recovery (single-column)) Suppose X is Bernoulli(θ)-Gaussian. For some positive constants α, c1 , and n0 , for all n > n0 , and for p > c1 n2 log2 n, if 2 α ≤ θ ≤ √ , (3) n n log n then, with an exponentially small probability of failure, the Algorithm ER-SpUD(SC) recovers all n rows of X. An additional factor of log n comes from the need for a gap between |b|(1) and |b|(2) of the k i.i.d. Gaussian random variables. On the other hand, using the sum of two columns of Y as r can save the factor of log n in the requirement on θ since the “collision” of non-zero entries in the two columns of X creates a larger gap between |b|(1) and |b|(2) . More importantly, the resulting algorithm is less dependent on the magnitudes of the nonzero elements in X. The algorithm using a single column exploited the fact that there exists a reasonable gap between |b|(1) and |b|(2) , whereas the two-column variant ER-SpUD(DC) succeeds even if the nonzeros all have the same magnitude.
